claim: Egypt forward Mostafa Zico, set up by Mohamed Salah, had a close-range goal disallowed by VAR while Egypt led 1-0, for an offence by Egypt defender Marwan Attia on Argentina defender Lisandro Martinez in the build-up. Reported timing is inconsistent across sources (the 58th, 62nd, and 67th minute have each been reported); Tier C and D sources cluster around the 62nd minute but this is not an official timestamp.
actual_decision: goal disallowed for an offence in the build-up
alternate_decision: goal stands; immediate score becomes Argentina 0, Egypt 2
law_reference: IFAB Laws of the Game, Law 12 (holding an opponent and standing on an opponent foot are each direct free-kick offences); disallowal follows the VAR protocol for an offence in the phase of play leading directly to a goal.
review_notes: A named former elite (Select Group) referee reviewing the match for ESPN (Andy Davies) called the disallowal correct, given the direct impact of the foul on an attacking sequence. This is Tier C qualified independent technical analysis, not a Tier A official record or a Tier B time-aligned video review performed by a project-appointed reviewer. Match commentary separately questioned whether the offence was within VAR remit at all, so part of the dispute is about protocol scope rather than only about whether a foul occurred. evidence_status stays reported and elapsed_seconds stays blank pending an official event log or a project reviewer with match video; the incident is correctly excluded from the primary counterfactual until then.

actual_decision: VAR checked both incidents and did not award a penalty
alternate_decision: penalty awarded on one or both incidents; branch to scored and missed outcomes
law_reference: IFAB Laws of the Game, Law 12; both appeals were reviewed under the VAR handbook penalty-incident protocol rather than left unchecked.
review_notes: The same Tier C ESPN technical review (Andy Davies) describes the Mac Allister and Fathy contact as minimal and the Alvarez and Salah contact as boot against boot with Salah going down unnecessarily, and calls both correctly cleared. This is one qualified analyst opinion, not a two-reviewer sign-off performed by this project, and there is no cited tournament-specific penalty-conversion source yet. evidence_status stays reported; a penalty scenario also needs elapsed_seconds and a documented conversion distribution (Project.md S7.4) before it can enter the primary counterfactual.
